ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a common center point, with 5 triangles radiating outward around it. Each triangle has the center point as one vertex, and its other two outer vertices each have an angle arc marked, so there are 5×2=10 marked angles in total. The angle at the center point in each triangle is not marked. The 10 edges emitted from the center point in the figure lie pairwise on the same straight line, forming 5 lines passing through the center point, so the 10 small angles around the center point can be viewed as 5 groups of alternate angles. Reasoning: Let the angles at the center point in the 5 triangles be c1,c2,c3,c4,c5. For each triangle, the sum of the three interior angles is 180°, so the sum of the two marked outer angles of that triangle is 180°−ci. Adding the 5 triangles together, the total sum of the 10 marked angles is (180°−c1)+...+(180°−c5)=5×180°−(c1+...+c5). Since these 5 center angles are alternate angles formed by 5 lines passing through the center point, their sum is 180°. Therefore the sum of the marked angles is 900°−180°=720°.

method.method_draft: Label the five triangles radiating from the common central point. From the image, each triangle has exactly two marked outer angles, making 10 marked angles total, and one unmarked angle at the shared center. Let the five central angles be c1,...,c5. For each triangle, the two marked angles sum to 180° minus its central angle, so the total marked sum is 5·180° − (c1+...+c5). Use the diagram’s straight-line structure through the center: the five central angles belonging to the triangles are alternating angles around a point formed by five straight lines, so their sum is 180°. Therefore the marked-angle sum is 900° − 180° = 720°.
